canonical_statement: The review aimed to assess the benefits and limitations of different SGLT2 inhibitors for cardiovascular and renal outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Therefore, we performed a network meta-analysis to assess the benefits and limits of different of SGLT2 inhibitors for cardiovascular and renal outcomes in patients with T2DM.

canonical_statement: The systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-NMA and registered in PROSPERO as CRD42020202202.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This systematic review article was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA-NMA).

canonical_statement: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to 11 November 2021, limited to English-language articles.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane library was performed from database inception to 11 November 2021

canonical_statement: Eligible studies were randomized clinical trials comparing an SGLT2 inhibitor with placebo or another glucose-lowering treatment.

population.label: Eligible randomized clinical trials
inclusion_criteria: Randomized clinical trial comparing an SGLT2 inhibitor with placebo or another glucose-lowering treatment

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged at least 18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus and HbA1c 6.5% to 10.5%.
Eligible trials required medication duration of at least 13 weeks and at least one cardiovascular or renal outcome.

population.label: Eligible trial populations
inclusion_criteria: At least one cardiovascular or renal outcome

canonical_statement: The review excluded type 1 diabetes or hereditary glucose/galactose malabsorption, trials without specified eligibility criteria, repeated secondary analyses of the same data, and preclinical animal research.

population.label: Excluded populations/studies
exclusion_criteria: Type 1 diabetes mellitus or hereditary glucose/galactose malabsorption
Repeated use of data for secondary analyses

canonical_statement: Trial selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two authors, with duplicate quality evaluation and disagreement resolution by additional reviewers.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Trial Selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two authors (LT and SA)

canonical_statement: Cardiovascular outcomes included cardiovascular mortality and hospitalization for heart failure.

outcome.definition: Cardiovascular mortality and hospitalization for heart failure

canonical_statement: The Methods section defined the renal composite as doubling of serum creatinine, initiation of renal-replacement therapy, or renal death.

outcome.definition: Doubling of serum creatinine, initiation of renal-replacement therapy, or renal death

canonical_statement: Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool across randomization, blinding, allocation concealment, and reporting-bias categories.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The quality of the included studies and risk of trial bias were assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool

canonical_statement: A frequentist network meta-analysis used hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals, the netmeta package in R 4.1.2, indirect comparisons, and P-score rankings from 0 to 1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used frequentist network meta-analysis. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used

canonical_statement: The search identified 4,170 records; 2,097 remained after duplicate removal, 89 underwent full-text review, and 10 trials were included.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: There were 4,170 records identified ... leaving 89 records for full-text review. Among them, ten trials were included

canonical_statement: The included network comprised CANVAS, CANVAS-R, CREDENCE, DECLARE-TIMI 58, DAPA-CKD, DAPA-HF, EMPA-REG OUTCOME, VERTIS-CV, SCORED, and SOLOIST-WHF.
The Results section reported 67,823 patients with T2DM randomized to an SGLT2 inhibitor or comparator.
CREDENCE, SCORED, and DAPA-CKD were described as enrolling patients with T2DM and kidney disease; SOLOIST-WHF and DAPA-HF were described as enrolling patients with T2DM and heart failure.
All included trials compared an SGLT2 inhibitor with placebo.

canonical_statement: The P-score ranking for all-cause mortality was Empagliflozin > Dapagliflozin > Canagliflozin > Ertugliflozin > Sotagliflozin.
The P-score ranking for cardiovascular mortality was Empagliflozin > Canagliflozin > Dapagliflozin > Sotagliflozin > Ertugliflozin.
The P-score ranking for hospitalization for heart failure was Canagliflozin > Empagliflozin > Sotagliflozin > Ertugliflozin > Dapagliflozin.
The P-score ranking for renal composite outcome was Dapagliflozin > Empagliflozin > Canagliflozin > Sotagliflozin > Ertugliflozin.

The authors concluded that dapagliflozin was most likely to have the best renal composite outcome ranking, while empagliflozin ranked best for cardiovascular mortality and canagliflozin ranked best for heart-failure hospitalization.
The authors identified heterogeneity across trials arising from clinical settings and national/ethnic groups.
The authors noted differences in baseline renal function across trials that could affect renal outcomes.
The authors noted that cardiovascular-risk definitions were inconsistent across included trials.
The conclusion claimed that dapagliflozin and canagliflozin showed prominent renal and cardiovascular effects compared with similar SGLT2 inhibitors.
The conclusion stated that SGLT2 inhibitors reduced all-cause mortality and showed benefits regardless of patient sex or diabetes status.
The authors stated that original contributions were included in the article and supplementary material and that inquiries could be directed to corresponding authors.

canonical_statement: The renal-composite definition is inconsistent: Methods define a narrower composite of creatinine doubling, renal-replacement therapy, or renal death, while the abstract/results use a broader composite including albuminuria/CKD worsening, ESRD, and transplant.

Renal-composite HRs for ertugliflozin and sotagliflozin conflict within the source: Results prose reports 0.70 (0.54-0.90) and 0.66 (0.56-0.77), while the abstract and Supplementary Table 2 report 0.81 (0.63-1.04) and 0.71 (0.46-1.09), respectively.

The main Results text describes DAPA-HF as enrolling patients with T2DM and heart failure, while Supplementary Table 1 labels DAPA-HF as 'no diabetic with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction'.
The network topology is placebo-centered; the active-agent rankings therefore depend substantially on indirect comparisons rather than direct head-to-head randomized evidence.
